newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big Loral call holder rolls up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Big Loral call holder rolls up.

text.p: Two weeks after opening a big position in the Loral Space & Communications Ltd January 1997 15 calls, an investor rolled them up to the 17-1/2 strike price on Wednesday, traders said.

By 1430 CDT (1950 GMT), 21,694 of the Loral January 15 calls traded, nearly all its open interest. At the same time, 20,216 of the January 17-1/2 calls traded. That option had open interest of about 1,465.
Loral shares, boosted by news it agreed to buy AT&T Corp's SkyNet Satellite Services, were up 2-1/4 at 15-1/2 on consolidated volume of more than 5.2 million shares.
Traders said Morgan Stanley, the brokerage that originally sold the 20,000 January 15 calls, was the firm that traded the 15-17-1/2 call spread.
"Morgan crossed the entire trade," one trader said.

John Streibich, a market maker on the Chicago Board Options Exchange, said the investor, who had opened the position by selling 20,000 of the January 15 calls, covered that short position and rolled out to the January 17-1/2 calls.
The spread crossed in three blocks, two of 9,000 contracts each and one of 2,000.
The January 15s traded at 1-7/8 and the 17-1/2s traded at 13/16. Morgan Stanley had initially sold the 20,000 January 15 calls at 3/4 on September 11.
In other activity, options on several technology stocks were active as the sector rallied sharply.
Iomega Corp extended recent gains, adding 3-3/4 to 23-3/4 on nearly 20 million shares. More than 50,000 Iomega options traded.
According to one trader, Iomega's average daily volume is in the 10,000 to 15,000 range.

The stock continued to rally on bullishness over the company's Zip drive, traders said. The bulk of the Iomega options traded on the American Stock Exchange, where more than 6,200 of the October 22-1/2 calls led the action. About 4,200 of the October 20 calls traded.
Traders said investors were buying calls and puts in every series. Iomega has options that expire in October, November, February and May.
Elsewhere, Micron Technology Inc options continued active on the Pacific Stock Exchange and CBOE as that stock also extended its recent gains.
Micron shares gained 1-1/4 to 32-3/4 on 9.5 million shares.
A rally in shares of 3Com Corp touched off heavy call buying, particularly in the January series, traders said.
"They're buying a lot of January stuff," one trader at the Pacific Stock Exchange said. "Everybody's trading it."
The 3Com January 60 call led the way, with about 9,650 contracts changing hands. The option was up 4-7/8 at 9-7/8.

3Com shares rallied 7-3/4 at 64-3/8 after the company posted better-than-expected first quarter earnings. Traders said 3Com helped boost Cisco Systems, which rose 2-3/4 to 63-1/4. --Gregory Crawford, 312 408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters
